Hi Connor,

Thanks for the quick intake last week. We're ready to onboard as a new supplier but have a couple of operational questions before we submit our first invoice:

1) Preferred invoice channel: our AR team normally emails invoices to partners (PDF + PO number in body). Do you require use of a vendor portal instead? If so, can smaller recurring invoices (under $500) still be sent by email?

2) PO matching: will our invoices need a 3-way match (PO + receipt + invoice) or do you use invoice-to-PO matching only? What variance tolerance should we expect (price/qty differences)?

3) Invoice format: do you need GL/charge codes on the supplier invoice, or will Redwood map to your chart of accounts? If there is a sample template we should use, please send it.

I've attached our completed vendor onboarding form (blueleaf_vendor_onboarding_form.pdf) and a sample invoice (sample-invoice.xlsx) for your review.

Appreciate any guidance — we want to make the first submission frictionless.

Thanks,

Hi Alex — welcome, and thanks for the form. Short answers up front, then details and a small checklist so your AR team can align: 

High level
- Preferred channel: Redwood's portal is preferred for all invoices where a PO exists and/or the invoice is > $1,000. Portal gives faster PO matching and traceability.
- Email fallback: acceptable for invoices under $1,000 or when the vendor does not have portal access. If emailed, please copy billing@blueleaflogistics.com and include the PO number in both the subject and the PDF body.
- PO matching: we do a 3-way match for physical goods and purchase orders that reference receiving. For services (SOW/time & materials), we perform a 2-way match (PO + invoice).

Matching tolerances (operational rules)
- Price variance tolerance: 2% per line item. If a line price deviates >2% from the PO unit price, the invoice moves to exceptions.
- Quantity tolerance: +/ -1 unit for countable items; anything else will flag for review.
- Tax/shipping: allowed to vary; flagged only if >$50 discrepancy relative to PO expectation.

Exceptions routing and SLAs
- Auto-route to AP exceptions queue when variance triggers. AP will try to resolve within 3 business days; if unresolved after 7 days it escalates to Procurement (Marissa copied).
- PO-less invoices over $2,000 require procurement approval before payment.

Template & required fields (if emailing)
- Required on every invoice: Redwood PO number, invoice number, invoice date, itemized lines with unit price and qty, remit address, and remit email.
- GL codes: optional on vendor side. Redwood will map to internal GLs. If you can include our project or cost-center code in the invoice (we'll provide the code on the PO), that speeds routing.

Attachments: I attached our vendor onboarding checklist and a short 'email-to-portal' quick reference for vendors (internal). I'll upload the preferred sample template to the supplier portal link and share.

Checklist for your AR before first invoice
- Confirm PO number is on the PDF and in the filename (e.g., Redwood_PO_123456_invoice_001.pdf)
- If invoice < $1,000 and emailed: send to payables@redwoodinference.com and cc: connor@redwoodinference.com
- Include one attachment only (invoice PDF). If supporting docs required, attach as a single ZIP or reference the portal upload.

I'll loop Marissa on escalation rules / procurement approvals. Let me know if you'd like a short walkthrough of the portal (15 min).

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Vendor Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachments: vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

Looping in procurement details so expectations are clear on the vendor setup side. A few operational items we need to confirm from Blueleaf: 

1) Payment terms: does Blueleaf accept Net30 by default, or do you have mixed terms by site? We need this field on your onboarding form. If you require Net45, mark it and note any discount terms.

2) Portal access & SFTP: if you prefer not to use the portal, we can temporarily enable SFTP ingestion for high-volume suppliers. For SFTP we require filename conventions and an SFTP account request form.

3) Auto-approval thresholds: we maintain an auto-approve threshold for recurring utility and low-dollar service invoices up to $750 (no PO). Does Blueleaf have recurring lines we should flag so we don't create repeated exceptions?

Operational ask for Connor/Marissa: when a PO-less invoice hits AP exceptions and is < $2,000, can we have AP auto-approve after 5 days if no procurement response? Marissa — can you confirm whether Procurement wants to keep that window or shorten it for new suppliers?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Procurement | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — clear and helpful. Quick responses: 

- Blueleaf default is Net30 for standard accounts; one of our shipping sites operates Net45 but we'll add that to the onboarding form per site.
- We'll target portal uploads for any invoice >= $1,000 and keep email for under $1,000 while portal access is provisioned.
- We'll mark our two recurring monthly service lines (warehouse slotting fees) so they can be auto-approve candidates up to $750.

Request: could someone share the portal sample invoice template and the filename convention you prefer for SFTP? If easier, we can schedule the 15-min walkthrough tomorrow.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll get the onboarding form updated and send first invoices next week.
